clue.text: Golf club in which food is provided between rounds

definitions.meaning: Royal St George's, an Open Championship venue on the Kent coast, is the golf club at this town

definitions.text: in which food is provided between rounds
definitions.meaning: a snack where a filling sits between two rounds, ie slices, of bread

explanation.surface: A golf clubhouse that lays on refreshments between rounds of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' looks like rounds of golf, but in the second sense it means rounds of bread, ie slices.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town gives its name to a famous links club, and the snack of filling between slices of bread bears the same name.

clue.text: Part of letter from a person who posted it, say

indicators.note: say indicates the words are taken as spoken, sounding like the entry

parts.note: one who posted the letter is a sender, with the article a

explanation.surface: Part of a letter from whoever posted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' means a written character, not mail: the stroke of b or d rising above the line.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography it is the stroke of a lowercase letter like b, d or h that rises above x-height.

clue.text: Boxing title, oddly, initially defended against amateurs

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the other letters wrap round the jumbled title
initially picks the first letter of defended

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: oddly tells us to rearrange the letters of title

explanation.surface: A boxing title strangely defended against people who are not professionals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing; 'oddly' is an anagram signal, not a pick of odd letters. Note the Italian plural ending in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilettanti are dabblers who pursue the arts for pleasure, not as professionals.

clue.text: Not being present for a term of Latin

definitions.meaning: said of someone absent, eg sentenced while away
the expression is Latin, used in legal English

explanation.surface: Absent for a whole term of Latin classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' suggests a school term of Latin lessons, but it means a Latin expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in someone's absence, ie while not there.

clue.text: Prisoner of ancient army a long time

parts.note: host is an old word for an army
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A captive of an army from long ago, held for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held as security for the fulfilment of demands.

clue.text: Flap endlessly, like wings

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is dropped from the word for flap

parts.note: a flap is a panic, ie alarm

explanation.surface: A bird beating its wings without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like wing movement but is a panic: ALARM, with 'endlessly' removing its M.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a technical adjective meaning relating to or shaped like wings.

clue.text: It may be played — but not in live performance, apparently

definitions.text: It may be played — but not in live performance, apparently

parts.words: It may be played — but not in live performance, apparently
parts.note: looks like a piece of music or a role, but refers to an animal whose name is played in the idiom for feigning death, so not live

explanation.surface: Something performed, though never on a live stage.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'play' this creature is to pretend to be dead or asleep, hence 'not live'.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing dead is the idiom built on this marsupial's habit of feigning death when threatened.

clue.text: Pilgrim and storyteller cooked salmon outside

indicators.note: outside means the salmon word goes round the word for cooked

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon
done means cooked through

explanation.surface: A pilgrim who tells tales while cooking salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym here. The Pardoner is one of Chaucer's Canterbury pilgrims.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales one pilgrim, a seller of indulgences, tells a tale.

clue.text: Part of US seen by many on stage

definitions.meaning: a state of the USA in the south-central plains
the Rodgers and Hammerstein musical, staged countless times

explanation.surface: A region of America that crowds have watched in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an American state and the title of a hugely popular stage musical.

clue.text: Mate's turned back, skirting constant danger to shipping

indicators.note: skirting means going round, so the reversed letters surround the constant
turned back tells us to write the word for the mate's letters in reverse order

parts.note: a mate is an ally, so mate's gives ally's
C is a common symbol for a constant, eg the speed of light

explanation.surface: A friend turns away, steering round a persistent hazard for ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' turns ALLYS into SYLLA, and 'skirting' puts C inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the six-headed monster on the rock opposite Charybdis threatened every passing ship.

clue.text: Reinforced, yet reversed course -

parts.note: yet in the sense of however gives but

indicators.note: reversed tells us to write the course's letters backwards

parts.note: a course of a meal, here the sweet one at the end

explanation.surface: Strengthened, though the route was turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns DESSERT into TRESSED. 'Course' suggests a route, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that is propped by supporting piers or braces has been strengthened.

clue.text: Prepare to publish part of screed I typed

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Getting a stretch of a long piece of typing ready for print.
explanation.definitionFit: Revising and correcting text is what is done to make it ready for publication.

clue.text: Napoleon's shopkeeper at home in castle

definitions.meaning: Napoleon is said to have called Britain a nation of shopkeepers
the proverb says a Briton's home is his castle

explanation.surface: A French emperor's merchant who lives in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves allude to sayings: Napoleon's jibe about a nation of shopkeepers, and the proverb that this man's home is his castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of England is the shopkeeper of Napoleon's jibe and the man whose home is his castle in the proverb.

clue.text: Cow I had, sheltered by friend

indicators.note: sheltered by means placed inside the word for friend

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A farmer's cow, kept in by a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal but is the verb to cow.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission.

clue.text: Cheer pilot for repairing this?

indicators.note: repairing means putting the letters of cheer pilot back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Encouraging a pilot fixing an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition and wordplay: 'repairing' rearranges CHEER PILOT, and a pilot would fix this.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary-winged aircraft is what a pilot would fly and want repaired.

clue.text: Term in Oxbridge college

definitions.meaning: the Oxford summer term after Easter bears this name
both Oxford and Cambridge have a college of this name

explanation.surface: A term spent at a college of Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's summer term and colleges at both ancient universities are named after the Holy Trinity.

clue.text: Like a sensitive soul, so to speak, hard to handle

definitions.text: Like a sensitive soul, so to speak
definitions.meaning: soul sounds like sole, and a sensitive sole of the foot reacts to a feather
delicate or tricky to deal with

explanation.surface: A touchy person who is difficult to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' says soul is to be heard as sole, the underside of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means reacting to being touched lightly, and also tricky or delicate.

clue.text: With time moved forward, sell art that's outstanding

indicators.note: moved forward tells us to shift that letter nearer the front of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to an art dealer to bring the sale date forward and sell some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With time moved forward' takes the T at the end of SELLART and moves it up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar performance means star quality, so the word is used for anything exceptional.

clue.text: Border on driveway

definitions.meaning: to come close to, verge on
the road leading up to a house

explanation.surface: A hedge beside the drive.
explanation.definitionFit: To come near to something, and the access road to a building, share the word.

clue.text: Take temperature inside and it's unusually cold

indicators.note: inside places that letter within the rearranged letters
unusually means the letters of and it's appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Checking the thermometer and finding an unusual chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes DISAN from AND IT'S, and T goes 'inside'. 'cold' means aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant manner is cool and unfriendly, keeping people at arm's length.

clue.text: Political system, as is covered by at Marx, primarily

indicators.note: covered by puts the small word inside the letters for the leading letter of Marx

parts.note: the first letter of the name Marx is a capital M
taken as written

explanation.surface: An economic order of the kind dealt with chiefly by Karl Marx.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx, primarily' looks like a first-letter pick giving just M, but the leading letter of Marx is a capital M. Marx's 'Das Kapital' makes the clue read as a plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic and political order based on private ownership of capital, the system Marx critiqued.

clue.text: One with home in Hundred Acre Wood, something difficult to rent

definitions.text: One with home in Hundred Acre Wood

parts.note: a pig of a job is something difficult
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A forest home that is hard to rent out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hundred Acre Wood is the setting of A.A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The small pink friend of Pooh lives in a beech tree in the Hundred Acre Wood.

clue.text: Text secretary finally put on PC

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the final letter follows the policeman

parts.note: PC is a police constable, slang cop

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word secretary

explanation.surface: An office worker eventually types something up on the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests a personal computer, but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Copy is printed or written matter, the text an editor or journalist works on.

clue.text: Laid down the law in cricket side I criticised

parts.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs
to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A captain blustering about being slated by his own cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is divided into the off side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Making laws is literally laying down the law, rather than the idiom for being bossy.

clue.text: Writer whose sister had one?

definitions.meaning: Charles of this name was an essayist who wrote as Elia
his sister was Mary, and in the nursery rhyme Mary had a little one

explanation.surface: An author whose sister owned something.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles's sister Mary co-wrote 'Tales from Shakespeare'; the nursery rhyme 'Mary had a little...' supplies the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles of that surname is a writer, and the nursery rhyme gives Mary a young sheep.

clue.text: Like carrier lost at sea, perhaps

parts.note: like in the sense of in the manner of gives as
a tray carries dishes or drinks

explanation.surface: A ship or aircraft carrier missing at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests an aircraft carrier but is a humble tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is off course has gone wrong or wandered, which is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Spice mixed by servants, for example

indicators.note: mixed tells us to jumble the letters of spice

parts.note: men in the sense of servants or workers

explanation.surface: Servants blending spices in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges SPICE to SPECI.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a single sample or instance taken as representative.

clue.text: Her yacht was at sea, as a rule

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman's yacht usually went out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was at sea' rearranges HER YACHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means government by a god or gods, a form of rule.
